articles.title_orig: iOS 27.2 adds two FaceTime features, including a personal favorite
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.2 adds two FaceTime features, including a personal favorite
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.2 adds new features to Messages , Podcasts , Photos , and more—including some easy-to-miss upgrades to FaceTime. Here’s what’s new.
Dual Capture was added to FaceTime in iOS 27 and quickly became one of my favorite features. Rather than having to choose between showing your face or the rear camera view, Dual Capture lets you show both at once.
iOS 27.2 expands Dual Capture to work on all video calls, even with groups. Previously the feature was limited to one-on-one calls.
If you have an iPhone 17 or newer, all you have to do on a video call is hit the ‘Flip’ button, and by default both the front and back camera will be activated.
It’s a huge upgrade to the FaceTime experience, and especially great if, like in my case, you have young kids running around and want to let grandparents see them and you at the same time.
The only drawback: everyone in the call needs to have iOS 27, iPadOS 27, or macOS 27 installed.
iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime more accessible by adding support for third-party sign language interpreters and live captioning.
Inside the three-dot icon, you’ll find a ‘Sign Language’ button that lets you pick an installed VRS (Video Relay Service) app for direct access to an interpreter. The app will appear as a participant tile in the call with a “Waiting for Interpreter” status, then your interpreter’s name will display after they join.
For third-party live captioning, Apple has a step-by-step support document here that outlines the process. You can also optionally stick with the existing built-in Live Captions feature to have your iPhone add automatic captions. It’s available from Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ FaceTime ⇾ Live Captions.
If you have an iPhone Duo, iOS 27.2 also introduced a new Edge Light feature that works across multiple video calling apps, including FaceTime.
Edge Light works just like on the Mac , adding a ring of light around the iPhone Duo display to better illuminate your face on calls. It’s a built-in alternative to using a physical ring light.
To enable the feature, open Control Center while on a FaceTime call then hit ‘FaceTime Controls’ and tap ‘Edge Light.’ Once enabled, you can adjust settings like the intensity and color temperature.
Have you tried any of iOS 27.2’s new FaceTime features? Let us know in the comments.

Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.
Like a real-life episode of “Suits,” the demise of famed white-shoe Wall Street law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges has been the talk of the legal industry this week. And now Silicon Valley has entered the picture.
Two-year-old AI-first law firm Crosby has put in a bid to buy some of the assets of Weil Gotshal, including its trademark, its brand, and some unspecified internal data, TechCrunch has confirmed. Separately, it is also working to hire some of the firm’s 1,200 lawyers. The Information was first to report this offer.
The once-prestigious Weil Gotshal confirmed to the New York Times this week that it was preparing to vote on dissolution in the coming days. The wind-down is happening after the firm’s presumed leadership heir apparent turned down the role, a number of its top-producing lawyers left, and a hoped-for merger with its rival, Willkie Farr & Gallagher, was shelved, the Times reported.
Meanwhile, Crosby’s founders believe they are the future of law firms. Rather than selling their internally developed AI tech to existing firms like Harvey or Legora, Crosby is an actual law firm. It uses its AI to provide legal services at, the startup promises, a speed never before possible.
The startup has raised about $85 million, including a $60 million Series B round in March led by Lux and Index, with participation from its seed-lead Sequoia, Elad Gil, 01 Advisors, and Bain Capital Ventures. Crosby came out of stealth mode in 2025 armed with $5.8 million in seed money.
While no one has pointed to the rise of legal AI as a contributing factor to Weil Gotshal’s downfall, AI may be key to the legal industry’s future. Terms of the bid weren’t disclosed and there’s no guarantee that Crosby will prevail. But if it does, Weil Gotshal’s legacy could somehow rise from the ashes, transformed by an AI-first firm.

articles.title_orig: Think tank: 114 companies paid no current federal income tax but still aren’t biggest hit to deficit
articles.title_zh: Think tank: 114 companies paid no current federal income tax but still aren’t biggest hit to deficit
articles.content_orig:
Federal tax figures for three major US airlines have challenged claims by Senator Bernie Sanders about corporate income tax payments. In an article published October 24, 2026, View From The Wing examined the 2025 financial records of United Airlines, American Airlines and Southwest Airlines, highlighting differences between reported tax expenses, actual payments and other federal taxes.
The analysis found that United Airlines reported $33 million in federal income tax payments during 2025, although its financial statements recorded only $4 million in federal income tax expense. The distinction reflects differences between cash payments and accounting expenses, which can involve payments or refunds associated with other tax years.
American Airlines recorded $79 million in income tax expense for 2025, while United reported $953 million and Southwest recorded $122 million. The reported amounts were mostly deferred tax expenses rather than immediate cash payments, according to the analysis.
American Airlines generated $54.6 billion in revenue but earned just $111 million in profit during 2025. Its net profit margin was approximately 0.2 percent, illustrating the relatively narrow profitability of the airline business.
Historical operating losses also affect airline tax obligations. Businesses can generally carry qualifying tax losses forward to offset future taxable income, subject to applicable restrictions. For losses arising after 2017, the general rule limits deductions to 80 percent of taxable income.
Warren Buffett previously cited Richard Branson when describing the financial risks of operating an airline.
"Start as a billionaire and then buy an airline." Warren Buffett quoted Richard Branson.
Buffett also criticized the industry's historical profitability challenges in his 1996 investor letter.
He described how a "farsighted capitalist" should have done humanity a favor by shooting Orville Wright down at Kitty Hawk.
Aircraft depreciation represents another significant factor in airline taxation. Companies generally spread aircraft costs across their expected useful lives in financial accounting, while tax rules can allow deductions to be claimed much faster.
The 2025 tax law restored permanent 100 percent bonus depreciation for eligible property acquired after January 19, 2025. This provision allows airlines to deduct qualifying aircraft costs immediately for tax purposes, even when financing obligations remain outstanding.
Southwest's financial disclosures identified accelerated aircraft depreciation as a source of tax benefits brought forward into earlier periods. The airline also reported that its federal tax-loss asset increased during 2025 despite generating a profit.
Aircraft investment deductions have competing economic implications. Faster deductions can reduce the immediate tax burden and encourage investment, potentially supporting aircraft manufacturers, suppliers, employment and lower airfares. However, they can also postpone tax payments as airlines continue purchasing aircraft.
The analysis also highlighted federal taxes beyond corporate income taxes. According to US Department of Transportation reporting, American, United and Southwest together recorded approximately $2.45 billion in employer payroll taxes during 2025.
The fuel estimates use reported domestic fuel consumption and the federal commercial aviation fuel excise tax of 4.3 cents per gallon. The figures cover mainline operations for the estimated fuel tax amounts.
The article also questioned the broader corporate list cited by Sanders, noting that some entries were subsidiaries of other companies. CVS and PayPal alone disclosed more than $2.1 billion in federal cash income tax payments, according to the analysis.
Corporate tax figures also depend on how multinational businesses allocate profits across different countries. The analysis cited Disney's $1.2 billion in income taxes and HP's $535 million in reported payments as examples of companies with substantial tax contributions.

articles.title_orig: ‘Asleep at the wheel’: Wallace slams Trump over China spy report involving Nvidia CEO
articles.title_zh: ‘Asleep at the wheel’: Wallace slams Trump over China spy report involving Nvidia CEO
articles.content_orig:
Wallace shared “shocking” new reporting that she said may show Trump is “setting America up to be a great loser on the world stage.”
MS NOW’s Nicolle Wallace shared “shocking” new reporting from The New York Times, which she said could show that President Donald Trump is “asleep at the wheel in protecting U.S. national security.”
On Thursday’s “Deadline: White House,” Wallace discussed the Times’ “blockbuster” report about a Chinese businesswoman’s close relationship with Jensen Huang , president and CEO of Nvidia, the world’s most dominant leader in artificial intelligence chips. U.S. officials concluded the woman was a Chinese intelligence asset, according to the report.
“The discovery that Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access to Mr. Huang, one of the most powerful figures in the A.I. revolution as well as an influential ally of President Trump’s, set off alarms at the White House,” the Times reported.
“What happened next,” Wallace said, “is the stuff of international political scandals.” The Times said Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings but chose not to act. He had “been wary of disrupting Nvidia’s chip sales, which are helping to drive the economy and the stock market, and of further complicating the trading relationship with China,” the report read.
“Donald Trump — the man who claims that no one is tougher on China than he is — does nothing,” Wallace said of the president’s reported inaction. She described “panic among our intelligence agencies as Trump sat by as a Chinese spy got dangerously close to the CEO of America’s most valuable company.”
Nvidia denied that its CEO had been targeted in a spy plot. The company told the Times that “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected” and that he “talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” The White House, the CIA and the National Security Agency declined to comment, according to the Times.
Wallace also pointed to “close financial ties” between Trump and Nvidia that were described in the report. A person familiar with the matter told the Times that Nvidia donated at least $20 million to Trump’s White House ballroom fund. Earlier this month, Trump disclosed that he bought up to $1.6 million worth of Nvidia stock and sold up to $1 million in August.
Wallace said the report exposed a gap between Trump’s public statements and private behavior.
“Earlier this year, he cited the importance of protecting America’s technological secrets and beating China in the AI arms race as his entire rationale for why AI can’t and should not be regulated ever,” she said.
By that logic, Wallace said, Trump is “setting America up to be a great loser on the world stage, as he imperils U.S. national security in a matter that’s deeply entangled in his own bottom line.”
You can watch Wallace’s full comments in the clip at the top of the page.

articles.title_orig: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
articles.title_zh: Outcry prompts ‘Call of Duty’ to cut Seoul tragedy footage
articles.content_orig:
American video game publisher Activision said Friday that it was removing controversial footage from its newly released “Call of Duty” game after an outcry in South Korea over the inclusion of real-life footage from a deadly 2022 Halloween crowd crush in Seoul.
Last week’s global release of “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” came days before the Oct. 29 anniversary of the disaster in the South Korean capital’s nightlife district of Itaewon, where a crowd of tens of thousands of partygoers surged beyond control in a narrow alley, causing nearly 160 deaths.
The game, which takes place amid a fictional North Korean invasion of the South, features about 10 seconds of heavily edited footage of the tragedy to illustrate what the aftermath of a Pyongyang attack might look like, though it does not refer to the Itaewon crowd crush directly.
Groups representing families of the crowd crush victims had demanded that the footage be removed, saying it was appalling that the game had directly reproduced actual scenes of people performing CPR “while victims lay on the cold streets amid chaos and desperation.”
“If the game developer has even the slightest sense of respect and empathy for the victims of the Itaewon disaster, it should promptly take corrective action,” the Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee said in a joint statement Friday.
The California-based game publisher, Activision, apologized in a statement and said the footage would be completely removed through a game update scheduled for release Nov. 12.
“This game is a fictional work created to provide a realistic and immersive experience,” the company said, according to the South Korean public broadcaster MBC. “In using actual news footage in the game, we never intended to evoke any tragic incident, including the Itaewon disaster, or to trivialize the suffering associated with such tragedies.”
The controversy came as grieving families are still waiting for answers about authorities’ failure to prevent the disaster four years ago. Nearly two dozen officials have been charged in the investigation, which is still underway, while three former police officers have been jailed.
On Thursday, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung vowed that his government would “uncover the truth.”
“On that day, when what should have been a joyful autumn night turned into the scene of a horrific tragedy, the state was nowhere to be found,” he said in a statement on X.
Lee Jin Woo, whose younger sister was 28 when she died in the crowd crush, told NBC News that he had played the new “Call of Duty” game and didn’t notice the Itaewon footage at first.
“But after hearing about it and thinking it over, I began to realize the footage looked very similar,” said Lee, who works at a South Korean gaming company.
“The more I thought about it, the more I felt betrayed as a gamer,” he said. “After all, it was a game company and a game series that I had liked.”
The game’s premise, in which South Korean conscripts are thrust into defending their country alongside American soldiers after a North Korean invasion, has been controversial since before it was available to play.
Though the “Call of Duty” invasion is fictional, it draws on North Korea’s real-life capture of Seoul in 1950 during the Korean War. The conflict ended in 1953 with an armistice instead of a peace treaty, and the two Koreas remain technically at war.
Tensions between the North and South have escalated in recent weeks, with the two countries embroiled in a standoff along their heavily militarized border. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has rebuffed diplomatic outreach from Washington and Seoul as he continues to advance his nuclear and ballistic missile programs.
“Ultimately, whether we’re talking about an actual war or the Itaewon disaster, both involve the suffering of real people,” Lee Mi Hyun, a director at the Itaewon Disaster Citizens’ Countermeasures Committee, told NBC News in an interview.
“They’re turning that suffering into entertainment,” she said. “It’s an approach that seems to show absolutely no empathy for the people who experienced that suffering.”
Some South Korean lawmakers say the game should be taken as a warning.
“We need to pay attention to the question it raises,” Han Dong-hoon, an opposition legislator, said last week in a Facebook post. “If that day were to come again, would we be ‘prepared’?”
The game has also been defended by members of Lee’s governing Democratic Party such as Kim Han Kyu, who said there was “nothing wrong with playing a game set against the backdrop of North Korea’s nuclear weapons.”
“We are still technically under an armistice, aren’t we?” he said Thursday in a Facebook post. “Wouldn’t it be even stranger if no games depicted a war against North Korea?”
Others have used the game to criticize Lee’s conciliatory approach to North Korea, with opposition lawmaker Ahn Cheol Soo suggesting last week that the South Korean president try playing the game to correct his “naïve judgment” about the North Korean threat.
With its “Call of Duty” franchise struggling to sustain interest in recent years, the Microsoft-owned Activision used “Modern Warfare 4” to deliver what fans loved about its previous games: a hyperrealistic military shooter.
“I don’t think we were happy with every aspect of last year’s game, and we heard the feedback loud and clear,” Activision Chief Marketing Officer Tyler Bahl told “The Game Business Show” earlier this month .
“With ‘Modern Warfare 4,’ we’ve tried to adjust based on that feedback. It’s getting back to a grounded military shooter. Making it cinematic, making it authentic and bringing that edge back that ‘Call of Duty’ is known for,” he said.
That approach appears to have worked. As of Friday, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4” was the top-selling game in both South Korea and the United States on Steam , an online PC game distribution platform.
In its review, gaming website IGN said it was a “much-needed reminder of what ‘Call of Duty’ can be at its best, even if it can’t fully recapture the heights of its glory days.”
Mithil Aggarwal is a Hong Kong-based reporter/producer for NBC News.
Stella Kim is an NBC News freelance producer based in Seoul.

articles.title_orig: AstraZeneca CEO strikes bullish tone on pipeline as stock rallies
articles.title_zh: AstraZeneca CEO strikes bullish tone on pipeline as stock rallies
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
AstraZeneca ( AZN ), Britain's biggest pharmaceutical company, said on Friday that its profit after tax rose 23% to $3.12 billion (€2.79bn) for the July to September period, driven largely by its cancer treatments.
That marks a sharp pick-up from the rise of just over 2% in the previous quarter. The firm also launched a plan to generate $1.5 billion (€1.34bn) in annual savings, which it intends to reinvest mainly in the drugs it has in development.
Revenue grew 7% to $16.2 billion (€14.5bn).
Oncology, its biggest business, accounted for 48% of the total, with sales up 17% to $7.8 billion (€6.99bn), led by lung cancer drug Tagrisso and immunotherapy Imfinzi. Core earnings per share, which exclude items such as restructuring costs and the amortisation of acquired drugs, rose 17% to $2.79.
The savings drive, called Reshaping for Sustainable Growth, will cost up to $2 billion (€1.79bn) in one-off restructuring charges and is due to be largely complete by the end of 2029.
AstraZeneca said the savings would be reinvested in the company, principally in its pipeline of new drugs, as it plans to "redeploy resources" across its existing business to back more than 180 projects in development.
Such restructuring could mean job cuts, though none have been announced.
"With multiple potential blockbuster assets in late-stage development and transformative technologies scaling rapidly, we are on track to deliver our 2030 ambition," CEO Pascal Soriot said in a statement.
The growth came despite pressure on older medicines.
Sales of Farxiga, its treatment for diabetes, heart and kidney disease, fell 25% to $1.6 billion (€1.43bn) after cheaper generic versions hit the US market, while blood thinner Brilinta also lost patent protection.
AstraZeneca is also facing volume-based procurement in China, a state bulk-buying scheme that forces drugmakers to cut prices in exchange for large orders.
US launches trade probe into Germany over medicine prices
Why pharma giant Roche is putting German investments on hold
The company confirmed its outlook for 2026, expecting revenue to grow by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core earnings per share by a low double-digit percentage, excluding currency swings.
It remains on track for its target of $80 billion (€71.7bn) in annual revenue by 2030, compared with almost $59 billion (€52.9bn) in 2025, and expects half of that to come from the US.
The company has been leaning further into the American market, adding a direct share listing in New York in February, while also pledging to invest $15 billion (€13.4bn) in China by 2030.
It has reported 12 positive results from late-stage trials so far this year, and is also developing a weight-loss treatment to compete with drugs such as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro.
AstraZeneca shares were up over 4.5% in early trading on Friday.

articles.title_orig: ExxonMobil and Chevron report blowout profits as Trump touts benefits of high oil prices
articles.title_zh: ExxonMobil and Chevron report blowout profits as Trump touts benefits of high oil prices
articles.content_orig:
It’s a good time to be an oil company.
The two largest U.S. oil companies, ExxonMobil and Chevron, on Friday reported blowout profits that easily beat expectations as oil prices remain sharply elevated because of the U.S. war with Iran.
ExxonMobil reported a profit that doubled from the same period last year, while Chevron’s earnings surged more than 180% from a year earlier.
As part of the bumper returns, Exxon said it was increasing the dividend it pays to investors.
The returns at both companies came as the price of oil surged beyond $100 per barrel and has remained there for months. On Friday, prices accelerated again, with Brent oil trading closing just under $118 per barrel.
The highest level that Brent reached since the United States and Israel launched the Iran war in late February was $126, which it is now approaching again.
Since the start of the year, Exxon shares have risen 52%, and Chevron shares have returned 50%.
Overnight, another major oil company, BP, reported that its profit skyrocketed to an 18-year high.
The average price of regular gasoline has soared 40% for consumers since the war broke out. Soaring prices continue to pressure consumers ahead of the midterm elections, where voters have repeatedly said that prices and inflation are primary concerns.
In 2024, Donald Trump repeatedly pledged to drive energy costs down . “My plan will cut energy prices in half or more than that within 12 months of taking office,” the then-candidate said in September 2024, while adding that it would mean “gasoline below $2 a gallon.”
As of Friday, the average gasoline price is currently more than double that.
In recent rallies on the campaign trail, the president has celebrated the higher oil and gas profits. “I wonder if I should say this,” Trump mused aloud during a rally Oct. 24, before saying “our country is making hundreds of billions of dollars because of what’s happened in the Middle East.”
Trump touts U.S. oil business making ‘hundreds of billions’
“My people said, ‘Please don’t mention that, sir,’ because people are paying a little higher,” Trump continued. “But what we’ve done for this country, we’re making money like this country has never made before.”
“I don’t give a damn: I’m going to say it. We’re making a freaking fortune.”
The higher prices are also a result of the war between Ukraine and Russia following President Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion of his neighbor in 2022.
“There’s a lot of disruption happening in the world,” ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods told CNBC on Friday morning . “What you’re finding is because of the closure” in the Strait of Hormuz, “shipping has to find new routes around to continue to deliver the products that society desperately needs.”
“About half of Russia’s refinery capacity has been taken out from the Ukraine bombing,” he added.
“That shortage of refining capacity and availability to the world is what’s driving product prices as high as it is, and frankly, diesel is the key crunch point here because it is so critical to economic growth,” Woods continued.
Since the start of the year, the average nationwide price for diesel fuel has risen 78%. New York-traded diesel futures have soared 130% since the start of the year, likely indicating more price rises could still come at the pump.
Both Exxon and Chevron said that they were running their refineries at maximum output to continue making as much diesel as possible.
Trump has taken specific note of the impact that diesel could have on the economy. The administration has quickly issued multiple orders and policies in an attempt to bring prices down.
The president signed an order allowing more widespread use of an off-road dyed variety of diesel, has pressured European allies to release more of the diesel reserves into the global market, and has announced a deal with Putin for some of that country’s diesel supplies.
Trump’s latest move came last week, when he announced $150 million in Defense Production Act funding to “expand petroleum production, storage, and logistics at refineries across.”
The moves have not meaningfully brought prices down.
On Friday, Woods said his refineries were already being pushed to the limit. “We are at record levels of utilization for our refineries,” he said on CNBC.
“If you look at North America, we produce record volumes of diesel. That’s all been a function of trying to drive more product into the marketplace to meet that demand and to drive costs down.”

articles.title_orig: Binance Hack Sends Crypto Stocks Tumbling
articles.title_zh: Binance Hack Sends Crypto Stocks Tumbling
articles.content_orig:
Binance said Friday that a security incident impacted about $6.3 billion in client assets, with around $3 billion frozen on-chain, marking the largest crypto hack on record.
The company later added it began recovering assets impacted by the breach after pledging to cover losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users, which the company created in 2018 as a protection for clients in the event of a hack.
It wasn't clear how the attack took place. The world's largest crypto exchange initially said the hack may involve "a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." However, Co-CEO Richard Teng later said the attack involved a more complex process rather than the misuse of a single engineer's permissions.
The FBI said Friday it was aware of the incident and was in touch with "relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate ​potential impacts, ​and ⁠coordinate appropriate investigative steps."
It wasn't clear either who was responsible for the breach. But TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and AI investigations company, pointed to North Korean hackers as the potential culprits . "Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst," the company said in a post.
Blockchain data platform Chainalysis also said this appears "be the work of North Korean cybercrime group TraderTraitor . This group has repeatedly targeted the cryptocurrency industry, exchanges, DeFi protocols, and investors, to raise funds for the regime. We base our intelligence assessment on on-chain activity observed in the hours following the hack."
Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals while it overhauls its withdrawal security systems and has revoked the affected address authorizations, Teng said. The exchange is also working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the stolen funds, while deposits remain unaffected.
Binance co-founder Yi He said deposits remained unaffected and continued to operate normally, while the exchange was working on enhancements to its withdrawal service and related address controls. It expects to begin resuming withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.
"We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said.
The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group , Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack.
Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. Over the past several years, bad actors have also drained billions of dollars in crypto from decentralized exchanges.
This week's breach "proves our exact point in proposing regulations for crypto markets earlier this month," Michael Selig, chairman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, said Friday in a CNBC "Squawk on the Street" interview. The U.S. derivatives regulator on Oct. 5 proposed a framework that would effectively put crypto exchanges under federal government oversight — after Congress failed to approve legislation to regulate the asset.
"The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don't have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States. We want to offer a federal option to these exchanges to come and register with the CFTC, and they would be subject to the same sorts of cyber security safeguards that we have in our markets today," he said.
Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,187.60 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach.
Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin.

articles.title_orig: Toyota reveals five new lifted Woodland concepts, including the bZ electric SUV
articles.title_zh: Toyota reveals five new lifted Woodland concepts, including the bZ electric SUV
articles.content_orig:
Toyota introduced a new family of lifted, “adventure-ready” Woodland concepts based on the RAV4, Grand Highlander, Sienna, Crown Signia, and bZ electric SUV.
Toyota is the latest automaker to chase the highly profitable off-road market in the US, with plans to expand its “Woodland” lineup.
Although it already sells Woodland versions of the RAV4, Sienna, bZ, and most recently, the Grand Highlander, Toyota said the new family of concept vehicles is “designed for drivers who see adventure not as a destination, but a way of life.”
Toyota’s North American design studio, CALTY Design Research, designed the concepts to explore how some of its most popular nameplates can be used better on and off the road.
Each vehicle features Horizon Blue exterior paint, inspired by Toyota’s 1960s models, including the Stout, Crown, and Corona.
All new concepts also include an exclusive Woodland badge, plus a lift kit, large over-fenders, satin-black wheels, All-Terrain tires, two-tone paint on the roof and hood, a roof rack, and cross bars to top it off.
According to Toyota, the RAV4 Woodland Plug-In Hybrid and Sienna Woodland Concepts show how its “electrified and family-focused vehicles take on a more adventurous role.”
The electric Woodland bZ Concept “extends the Woodland theme into Toyota’s battery electric future.” Meanwhile, the Grand Highlander Woodland Concept and Crown Signia Woodland Concept bring two distinct models to the lineup, Toyota said.
The company didn’t reveal any powertrain specs or other details, but said the concepts show how capability can take many forms, including PHEV, hybrid, and battery electric.
Toyota’s new Woodland Concepts will be on display at the 2026 SEMA Show, starting on November 3.
To give you an idea, the 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower. That’s an extra 37 hp compared to the standard bZ with AWD.
The bZ Woodland also adds off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and the ability to tow up to 3,500 lbs.
Other rugged upgrades include All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.
The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

articles.title_orig: iPhone Duo Review: One Week Later
articles.title_zh: iPhone Duo Review: One Week Later
articles.content_orig:
It's been a week since the iPhone Duo was released, and MacRumors videographer Dan Barbera wanted to revisit his review since he's been able to use the Duo for a longer stretch of time.
None of us at MacRumors have had a display crack, and we've seen some AI photos floating around, so it's hard to tell just how many people are actually having problems. iPhone Duos with the hinge issue that causes the display to crack seem to get damaged shortly after purchase, so if you've had an ‌iPhone Duo‌ for the last week and it's still fine, it's not likely to have this defect.
The outer display is small, but Dan finds it useful for checking notifications, replying to messages, and scrolling through apps and websites. He unfolds it for multitasking or longer messages, and is a fan of using the ‌iPhone Duo‌ unfolded in portrait mode for watching videos and using an app at the same time.
He finds the Touch ID fingerprint sensor easy to find, and says Apple Watch unlock is similar to Face ID . The cameras are just okay, and someone who zooms in a lot is probably going to miss having a telephoto lens.
Battery life is between an iPhone 18 Pro and a Pro Max, and for most people, it's likely going to last a full day. Not all apps have been updated for the Duo layout yet, but it's getting better. There's an extension called Wider that extends the Safari window to the edges of the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s outer display, and it's a big improvement. We may see other accommodations in the coming months as developers and users get used to the new layout.
Dan says the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is the most excited he's been about an iPhone in a long time, and he plans to keep using it even though he misses having a telephoto lens.

articles.title_orig: North Korean hackers likelinked to record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
articles.title_zh: North Korean hackers likelinked to record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, was hit late Thursday by what investigators say is the biggest crypto hack in history , with $6.3 billion in funds impacted and roughly half of those assets frozen.
Customer withdrawals have been temporarily suspended, and co-CEO Richard Teng promised the exchange will cover all losses.
"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said on social media.
Binance said it has money set aside in a Secure Asset Fund for Users to handle extreme cases, such as security breaches.
Here's what you need to know:
Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a separate social media post Friday morning that customer withdrawals should resume within 48 hours.
"We are rebuilding the withdrawal service, and we are not switching it back until it passes rigorous testing," noted Teng on Friday. "We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to the Sunday deadline."
Teng said the hack was not carried out by one person. Initial findings pointed to a compromised laptop, but further review revealed broader security breaches.
"This was a complex attack," Teng said. "The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and tracers."
The attack has rattled crypto markets and related stocks. Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) tumbled 5% to hover below $77,000 on Friday.
Other major crypto assets also tumbled after the hack, with ether ( ETH-USD ) dropping 4% to around $2,200. Binance's native token, BNB ( BND-USD ), also plunged by more than 6%.
Crypto-related stocks traded lower, led by shares of Circle, trading platforms Coinbase ( COIN ) and Robinhood ( HOOD ), and digital-asset Treasury giant Strategy ( MSTR ).
Binance said that about $3 billion in assets have been "frozen on-chain so far."
The frozen assets include over $2 billion in stablecoins. Tether, the world's largest stablecoin issuer, "froze more than 1.567B" of its USDT stablecoin in relation to the hack," CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X . The second-largest issuer, Circle ( CRCL ), froze another $800 million "in coordination with law enforcement," CEO Jeremy Allaire said. World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency venture co-founded by President Trump and his sons, said it froze $27 million of its stablecoin, USD1, associated with the hack, according to CEO Zack Witkoff.
Although details are still emerging, the hack is shaping up to be the largest crypto theft in history, far exceeding the previous record set in February 2025, when attackers stole $1.5 billion from the crypto derivatives exchange ByBit.
Blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Elliptic have linked the theft to North Korean hackers, with TRM attributing it "with high confidence" to a group known as TraderTraitor, the same group responsible for last year's Bybit hack.
Elliptic estimated Friday that about 44% of the stolen assets have been frozen, with stablecoins accounting for nearly all of those funds. The firm estimated that attackers still controlled over $3 billion in crypto that token issuers cannot directly freeze.
The hackers appear to have compromised Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure, allowing them to authorize transactions that drained billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains, according to the firms. Binance, in its preliminary stage, has conducted an investigation into the hack, which suggests the incident may have begun with a compromised engineer's laptop. The exchange added that it has found no evidence that wallet passwords were leaked.
North Korean hackers swiped $2 billion in 2025 , bringing the rogue regime's total haul since 2016 through the end of last year to $6.75 billion, according to data from crypto firm Chainalysis.
"This is likely the largest crypto hack on record, but the key distinction is that it does not currently appear to be a solvency event for Binance," Fundstrat head of digital assets Sean Farrell said.
"That meaningfully reduces the risk of a negative feedback loop involving withdrawals, forced selling, tighter credit, and broader deleveraging," he added.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter at Yahoo Finance.
David Hollerith is a senior banking and finance reporter at Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X @DsHollers .

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Pakistan military 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Pakistan military 'cautiously optimistic' on Iran-US mediation
articles.content_orig:
Pakistan’s army is “cautiously optimistic” ⁠about mediation efforts between Iran and the United States as regional countries seek to revive a ceasefire in the eight-month-old war.
Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, spokesman for Pakistan’s military, suggested on Friday that there were positive signs in attempts to de-escalate the conflict. His comments to the Reuters news agency were the first since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.
Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan’s chief mediator, has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday, alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.
“Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive ⁠sign.
“The word that we would use is always cautiously optimistic,” added Chaudhry, director general of Inter-Services Public Relations.
He also warned that there are parties seeking to obstruct mediation between the US and Iran.
There are still “powerful spoilers and detractors” who believe conflict serves them, he added without naming them.
Speaking in the garrison city of Rawalpindi, where Pakistan’s armed forces are headquartered, Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed in Tehran or whether the US had backed the trip.
His comments on Friday came as Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran in another apparent bid to negotiate a revival of the June ceasefire that collapsed months later.
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin joined Pakistan’s Munir in ‌Tehran on Monday.
Their two countries signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan on August 7, saying an attack on any signatory will be treated as an attack on all.
The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement has taken on added significance as the Iran war has redrawn regional alliances and raised fears of a broader Middle East conflict.
While the three signatories say the agreement is aimed at collective deterrence and regional security, analysts see its evolution as closely tied to efforts by regional powers to manage the fallout from the Iran-US confrontation.
After Monday’s talks, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said regional security should be ensured by regional countries without foreign intervention.
The wording of the pact does not bar new ⁠members, Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join.
“Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence ⁠and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide.
Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership.
He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi ⁠Arabia and the holy sites of Mecca and Medina. “We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an intra-Yemen conflict,” he added.
Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group has been reignited by the Iran ⁠conflict, stoking fears of a wider war.

Video captures a massive rockfall near the Goreme Open-Air Museum in Turkey's popular Cappadocia region. The collapse occurred after heavy rainfall caused rocks to break away from a volcanic formation known as a ‘fairy chimney.’ (Source: Reuters)
At least three people were killed at Cappadocia, a popular tourist destination in central Turkey, when a rockfall occurred Thursday, officials said.
The rockfall took place at around 3:15 p.m. local time that day, according to Reuters.
After the area experienced heavy rain, the rockfall came from a volcanic geological formation called a "fairy chimney," the same source said.

The name comes from the tall, narrow, often cone-shaped rock formations that resemble chimneys, with the "fairy" reference tied to local folklore.
Rock fragments from the fairy chimney broke off and fell onto people near the Goreme Open-Air Museum , Nevsehir Gov. Huseyin Kok told reporters.
At least three people were killed, and five others were injured after a rockfall struck Cappadocia, a popular open-air tourist destination in central Turkey. (Ihlas News Agency via Reuters)
Three people died and five were injured, according to The Associated Press.

The deadly rockfall occurred around 3:15 p.m. Thursday near the Goreme Open-Air Museum, pictured. (Sercan Ozkurnazli/dia images via Getty Images)

articles.title_orig: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Case, Avoiding Trial
articles.title_zh: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Case, Avoiding Trial
articles.content_orig:
Meta on Friday reached a settlement with a teen plaintiff, identified in court documents as K.D.B., who claimed the company’s platforms, Instagram and Facebook, were addictive and caused her mental ‌health problems, attorneys for the plaintiff said.
The news comes just one day after the tech giant reached a settlement with S.J., the second teen plaintiff who had sued the company over similar claims. The terms of the settlement agreements with both plaintiffs are confidential.
In the weeks leading up to trial, TikTok and YouTube reached agreements to resolve the claims brought against them by both S.J. and K.D.B.
“We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client,” Emily Jeffcott, trial counsel for K.D.B., said in a statement.
Snap Inc. now remains the lone defendant in the trial, which began this week in Los Angeles with jury selection. Opening arguments are slated for Nov. 4.
In their lawsuit, K.D.B. and S.J. allege that Snap, the maker of Snapchat, designed features that would maximize the time young users spend on the app. Those features include Snapstreaks, Snapscores and filters that can trigger compulsive use of Snapchat, leading to severe mental and physical health issues like self-harm.
Meta settles social media addiction lawsuit for $18 billion
Their case is the fourth bellwether in a consolidated group of cases brought against Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Snap by more than 1,600 plaintiffs, including over 350 families and over 250 school districts. The plaintiffs accuse the tech companies of knowingly designing addictive products harmful to young users’ mental health.
Historically, social media platforms have largely been shielded by Section 230, a provision added to the Communications Act of 1934 that says internet companies aren’t liable for the content users post.
Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, has repeatedly denied that its apps are purposefully harmful and addictive for young users.
In March, during a landmark social media addiction trial in Los Angeles, a jury found Meta and Google’s YouTube negligent in the design or operation of their social media platforms.
The jurors determined that Meta’s and Google’s negligence was a substantial factor in causing harm to the plaintiff, identified in court by her initials, K.G.M., and that the companies failed to adequately warn users of the dangers of Instagram and YouTube, their respective platforms.
The jury awarded K.G.M. $3 million in compensatory damages, finding Meta 70% responsible for harm caused to the now-20-year-old plaintiff, and YouTube responsible for 30%.
In August, Meta agreed to settle a wide-ranging social media addiction lawsuit with the state of California and a number of other states for about $18 billion. The court filing says that the company “denies the allegations against it and that it has any liability to the Plaintiffs,” which are a collection of 29 states.
In a statement to NBC News on Friday, a spokesperson for Meta said the company will continue to defend itself in court and stand by its record.
“We’ve spent more than a decade building protections for teens, and our agreement with 52 bipartisan attorneys general goes even further with strict time limits, no access at night, and no notifications during school hours,” the statement read in part. “We hope the rest of our industry joins us in setting this new standard.”
A spokesperson for Snap on Friday sent NBC News its statement from earlier this week, which read, in part, “From the beginning, Snapchat was built differently from traditional social media: it opens to a camera, not a feed, not a ranking of what other people post or other social comparison metrics.”
“We have built safeguards into the platform, introduced safety tools and educational resources,” the statement continued, “and we believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs’ experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed.”
Alicia Victoria Lozano is a California-based reporter for NBC News focusing on climate change, wildfires and the changing politics of drug laws.

articles.title_orig: Tomb Raider (Game Boy) - 'The Editors Had to Retcon the Score Because It Was Higher than Pokémon and Zelda'
articles.title_zh: Tomb Raider (Game Boy) - 'The Editors Had to Retcon the Score Because It Was Higher than Pokémon and Zelda'
articles.content_orig:
This month sees the launch of the Making of Tomb Raider 1997-2000 book, an unofficial deep-dive into the creation of some of Lara Croft's most beloved adventures, written by me, Daryl Baxter .
In case you're keen for a taster of what the book might contain, I've included an excerpt which focuses on Lara's Nintendo debut, which took place on the Game Boy Color in 2000.
At this point, I'll hand over the mic to artist Matt Charlesworth , who was kind enough to speak with me about the creation of this beloved handheld title.
"After helping with Tomb Raider 3 via the loading screens, I got chatting with Sean Dunlevy , who had just finished working on Fighting Force 64 . We were both super excited about working on the newly released Game Boy Color, as it gave him a chance to get back to low-level ASM coding on simpler 8-bit systems, and it allowed me to learn an art form that was (at that time) dead on major home consoles and game systems: pixel art.
After a month or two of prototyping, Sean and I had the framework of a cartoony space adventure with similar gameplay to Flashback / Another World , called Salvage . It was at this point that we realised that we could make this into a pretty great portable TR game, so we met with [Core Design boss] Jeremy Smith and got the approval to do exactly that.
Sean and I started on that project for different reasons. I think he wanted to avoid the larger team sizes and codebase of the PS1 generation, and I wanted to have a place where I could rapidly learn new techniques to broaden my skill set without the stress and focus drawn by working on the flagship PS1 games. Sean was a seasoned veteran programmer by this time, and as I stated before, I knew very little but was eager to learn.
Teaming up with Sean was a great experience, and I’m lucky I had that experience with him in particular, as he was patient and great at explaining the technical things I needed to understand without ever patronising or talking down to me. I’m extremely grateful to him for that time.
Lightning then struck twice when we hired gameplay programmer Ian Manders from Rare – another incredible person who was a joy to work with. Despite being closer to my age than Sean, he brought with him a ton of experience from Rare, having shipped Donkey Kong Country games on Game Boy and Ken Griffey Jr.’s Winning Run on the Super Nintendo console.
Tomb Raider felt like a direct 3D evolution of games such as Prince Of Persia , Another World, and Flashback, so it seemed obvious to us that a 2D TR game should evoke similar mechanics and gameplay to feel authentic and on brand.
We made progress pretty quickly on the game, but it also became obvious really fast that I wouldn’t be able to do all of the art myself for the entire game – it was too much and I had too much to learn. I don’t remember exactly how it happened, but thankfully, at just the right time, a bunch of animation grads from Ballyfermot Animation College in Ireland arrived at Core, and we were able to pick Fergus [Duggan] and Paschal [McGuire] to add to our team.
Although Paschal struggled a little to transition into game development, Fergus was the right person we needed. He took on and owned the entire background art for the game and allowed me to focus on Lara and enemy art, and animation. He did an unbelievable job, and I think his work on both Game Boy games stands up to this day.
At the outset, I remember the legendary Jerr O’Carroll also assisting me with learning 2D pixel art and design as we explored the Salvage project, but he didn’t transition with us onto the Tomb Raider game, as I think he was animating on TR4 as far as I remember. But shortly after Fergus and Paschal joined us, Lee Pullen (whose pixel art defined the characters of the Chuck Rock series) also lent a hand and taught me a bunch about efficiently conveying motion with the extreme constraints of super low-res pixel art.
The thing I remember most from that time was working incredibly long hours and feeling way out of my depth, but having my late friend Troy Horton producing our game made it manageable, and thanks to him, we knew everything would be alright.
After probably about a year, we were done, and THQ published the game. We shipped that after about a year of incredibly hard work and crazy hours (all self-inflicted) and received at least one 10/10 review from a GB-specific print magazine at the time. It’s hilarious, but looking through that archive, I see that the editors of the magazine had to retcon the review score down after several issues because it was ranking higher than Pokémon and Zelda !
This was an incredibly rewarding game to work on, especially as it was my first real game I contributed to in a truly meaningful way, and because Sean and I ran the project and had full creative control."
The Making of Tomb Raider 1997-2000 is available now.

articles.title_orig: Exxon and Chevron report massive profits after Trump brags U.S. energy companies are ‘making a freaking fortune’ just before midterms
articles.title_zh: Exxon and Chevron report massive profits after Trump brags U.S. energy companies are ‘making a freaking fortune’ just before midterms
articles.content_orig:
Chevron and ExxonMobil on Friday reported profits that soared in the third quarter, as their U.S. refineries ramped up production to full capacity to take advantage of high diesel fuel prices.
Chevron shares are up nearly 2% while Exxon is more than 1% higher. Both touched all-time highs Friday.
The world is facing a fuel crisis as Ukraine, Iran and Houthi militants attack refineries in Russia and the Middle East, reducing global capacity by millions of barrels per day. Importers have increasingly turned to U.S. Gulf Coast refineries for diesel supplies as a consequence.
ExxonMobil's profits doubled to $15.4 billion, or $3.72 a share, compared to $7.5 billion, or $1.76 a share, in the same period in 2025. When adjusted for one-time items, it posted earnings of $4.23 a share, soundly beating Wall Street's expectations.
"Refining capacity is very tight today," Exxon CEO Darren Woods told CNBC in an interview. "Frankly, diesel is the key crunch point here because it is so critical to economic growth [with] very inelastic demand."
U.S. diesel stood at a national average of $6.32 per gallon on Friday, an increase of more than 70% compared to the same period last year, according to AAA. Prices in the U.S. hit a record high in September.
Chevron's net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion, or $5.06 a share, compared to $3.5 billion, or $1.82 a share, in the same period last year. When adjusted for one-time items, it reported earnings of $5.28 per share, also beating the Street's expectations of $4.89.
"The system is under stress," Chevron CEO Mike Wirth told CNBC in an interview. "We remain in an environment that is fairly fragile."
Here's what Chevron and Exxon earned, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:
High profits from the largest oil companies at a time of war is politically controversial. President Donald Trump said in August that Chevron and Exxon "were making too much money based on a shortage." The supply disruption began in March after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.
Profits from Chevron's refining division surged more than 300% to $4.9 billion compared to $1.1 billion in the same period in 2025. Its oil and gas production generated earnings of $5.7 billion, up 70% from $3.3 billion in the year-ago period.
Chevron's U.S. refineries processed record amounts of crude oil at just above 1 million barrels per day, as the facilities ran at 98% capacity. Diesel and jet fuel yields rose more than 10%, Wirth said.
Exxon's refining division generated profits of about $7.2 billion in the quarter, outpacing its production business' earnings of about $7.1 billion. Its refining profits have surged nearly 200% to $11.4 billion so far this year compared to $4 billion during the first nine months of 2025.
Exxon's Gulf Coast refineries operated at 100% capacity utilization. Those refineries produced "record volumes of diesel" in the quarter, Woods said.
Chevron's oil and gas production actually declined slightly to 3.9 million barrels per day compared to about 4 million bpd in the same period last year. The decline was in its international segment due in part to the conflict in the Middle East, while output was largely flat in the U.S. year over year.
Exxon has produced about 4.5 million bpd this year, a more than 2% decline from nearly 4.7 million during the first nine months of 2025.

articles.title_orig: We Must Kill Windows For A Just Future
articles.title_zh: We Must Kill Windows For A Just Future
articles.content_orig:
Nobody likes Windows. This cannot continue. We must come together and annihilate it. I hate to say it, but the way forward is Linux
You never use Windows because you like Windows–you use Windows because it is there. This has been true my entire life. I have lived through the operating system’s ups and downs, including Windows Millennium Edition, which was worse than you could imagine and, somehow, worse than its reputation. But while Windows 10 was sorta okay, Windows 11 is wretched. The day-to-day experience of using it has deteriorated into something dreadful. If we continue to enable Microsoft, the walls will decay and fester eternally. We must escape this cycle of pain together.
Microsoft as a company, minus many of the good gaming companies it bought and the employees at the margins allowed to make tiny useful pieces of software, is a rot plaguing the world. Be it its active aiding in the genocide in Gaza , its unhinged commitment to AI , or just the fact that Windows and the 365 Suite have always sucked a little to use, the compromise that has existed with regular people for a long time has disintegrated. To the extent that computing can be moral, a moral future must be one without Microsoft generally and Windows specifically. We cannot assume that Windows will collapse under its own mediocrity; if that were true it would have happened decades ago. We must kill Windows. We must cut it out from our lives like a tumor; we must systematically consider what we need from it and seek to construct alternatives with purpose. It turns out that’s still quite hard, but every single day the process is easier.
For clarity and as a point of policy, it is worth mentioning that while Xbox is the subject of a “priority boycott” by BDS, Microsoft generally is categorized as a “pressure target. ” These are slightly different asks, as the BDS movement itself acknowledges how difficult it is to divorce oneself from Microsoft either personally or vocationally, asking on its website to “consider switching [to] free and open software instead of another, possibly complicit company.” This is in part due to the insidious, rent-seeking nature of Microsoft that has wormed its way into the fabric of everyday life: It is easier to cancel your Game Pass account than it is to tell your boss you’re not using Teams or to install Linux Mint on a company laptop. It is not a personal failing to be required to use Windows for your job.
Aftermath reached out to BDS, who provided us with the following statement about the boycott. Here it is in full.
But it is not just BDS making the call for alternatives, as many people outside of the United States understand that the hegemonic nature of US tech is itself a liability to everyone in the world. (My colleague Tech Won’t Save Us podcaster and author Paris Marx has written a guide about this that I quite like.) As the United States becomes increasingly erratic, other countries are realizing that they need an offramp. France’s Interministerial Directorate for Digital Affairs (DINUM) recently announced that they are in the process of transitioning to a version of NixOS called SécurixOS and are working to formulate a long term plan. "The State can no longer simply acknowledge its dependence; it must break free,” David Amiel, France’s minister of public action, said in a statement in April. “We must become less reliant on American tools and regain control of our digital destiny." Similarly, the Dutch government is also developing its own variant of NixOS called Digitaal Autonome Werkomgeving Overheid or Digital Automated Working Environment (DAWO ).
“The world has now seen very clearly how the US government and the billionaires of Silicon Valley will work together to wield the dependence of countries around the world on the US cloud, digital services, and social media platforms against them — even going so far as to completely cut off members of the International Criminal Court, the United Nations, and former European Union officials,” Paris Marx told me via direct message. “US tech companies and their government can no longer be trusted, and that makes dependence on US tech an inherent threat to sovereignty — not to mention the existing threats to a healthy society that have been accumulating for years. As long as that dependence continues, the United States can use it as a weapon.”
If complicity in a ongoing genocide was not enough, Microsoft has hitched its future on artificial intelligence. It is a move that is an existential risk to the economy, a security risk, and somehow the most annoying thing the company has ever done with its OS in its entire history. Microsoft is a key part of the cadre of useless jackasses making the computer expensive . Though Windows 11 had some nice additions at the beginning (Powertoys, Winget , the sound design), the experience itself has become garbage as they have shoved more and more half-broken shit into the operating system. Basically no person on Earth wanted the controversial Recall feature that took snapshots of your computer . Copilot is a nightmare that nobody seriously uses on an OS level, and Microsoft has said their goal long term is to get people “addicted” to their AI assistants . Microsoft’s very conception of what they envision the operating system becoming, an “ agentic OS ” is glassy-eyed, tech sector cult pablum masquerading as visionary and a direction I am fundamentally opposed to for a machine that I use to play Balatro and answer emails.
Every mandatory update to Windows 11 is a slot machine that might make your computer run like a dog that ate a bag of dark chocolate. It has gotten so bad that Microsoft’s chief of Windows Pavan Davuluri had to write a we-acknowledge-this-OS-sucks-ass blog to address how unusable and intrusive the entire rats nest has become, and made a commitment to do better . Not to call the man a liar, but I am going to tell you, as someone who had to interact with Windows for decades, that in the long run that isn’t going to happen. If you believe that even a little bit you are a rube and should consider your life choices.
There is a black hole at the heart of that company, and no minor gains that Windows claws back will ever make up for the inescapable gravity of Microsoft products getting shittier over time. They will extract rent from you and your employer at every plausible juncture and give you garbage in exchange. You must accept in your heart that Windows is a lost cause. Once you do, the work begins.
Around 2010 I remember waiting in line to get into PAX East and being approached by a guy handing out burned CDs. He was distributing copies of Linux, either Mandrake or Red Hat, to everyone waiting in line. Had I heard the good word? I had. I have tried many times before to divorce myself from Windows over the years, each time with varying success. I have existed between hardcore PC building and being a Mac person my entire life — a status that remains to this day in the hodgepodge of devices in my office.
From a purely conceptual perspective, the well-meaning dweeb handing out burned software in line has been vindicated. The arc of history is long and bends towards open source software. I should be clear that Linux is not morally good on its own; it can and often is used for evil ends. Linux has the same slop problem every other piece of software has, and Linus Torvalds needs an intervention over AI coding . But Linux is also free, and not simply in the monetary sense of the word.
I had tried installing Linux on my home PC back in the 2000s, but it didn’t stick the second I realized I couldn’t play Final Fantasy XI on it. I have lived on and off with elements of Linux in my life — multiple network devices I own run some variant of Debian Linux, I regularly had WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) enabled, and I have often put my machine in dual boot for specific use cases. I have two Macs and a PC at my desk and use the same unified shell for both. My choice

articles.title_orig: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
articles.title_zh: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
articles.content_orig:
European diplomats have refused to stand for an official photo with Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov at the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in the US, leading to the American hosts cancelling the planned picture.
Two officials confirmed to the BBC the cancellation of the so-called family photo scheduled for Friday morning, which would usually include representatives from all the nations in attendance.
The meeting, which gathers top diplomats from the world's biggest economies, is being hosted in Atlanta by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Ukraine is not not a G20 member but has been invited to similar meetings in recent years. However, Ukraine was not invited to this meeting.
Relations between Ukraine and the US have been particularly tense this month, with a diplomatic standoff between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Donald Trump over Kyiv's strikes on oil infrastructure within Russia.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is present and a diplomatic source confirmed the UK was among the countries which refused to participate in the picture.
One British official said: "The UK has a longstanding policy not to have direct, bilateral engagement with Russian ministers since the invasion of Ukraine and we are not about to change that".
A US official said the photo was cancelled "after it became clear some of the delegations were unwilling to participate in a joint photo".
"Rather than allow a ceremonial photo opportunity to become a diplomatic distraction, the US decided to forgo the photo and keep the focus on the substantive discussions," the official said.
In contrast to Ukraine, relations between the US and Russia appear to have partially thawed in recent weeks, as Trump waived some sanctions and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the American market.
The move comes as Trump attempts to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of mid-term elections at the start of November, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war.
Ukraine and its European allies have heavily criticised Trump's deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Zelensky called it "a gift" to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".
Trump said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Putin has said Russia, which introduced a ban on diesel exports earlier this year, is willing to supply both the US and global markets with oil and petroleum products.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and currently controls approximately a fifth of Ukrainian territory.
Moscow has in recent weeks intensified its deadly missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.

articles.title_orig: FCC Plans Vote To Block China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom From U.S. Phone Numbers
articles.title_zh: FCC Plans Vote To Block China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom From U.S. Phone Numbers
articles.content_orig:
Published 30 Oct 2026, 17:24 UTC
This article is an automated aggregation of coverage from news outlets. Our editorials offer in-depth analysis curated by the NewsCord team.
FCC to vote November 19 blocking Chinese telcos' direct access to US numbers Policy targets China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other IP-enabled service providers
The United States Federal Communications Commission plans to vote on November 19 on a proposal to block China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other internet-based service providers from direct access to American phone numbers. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said, "With this decision, the FCC will be strengthening our first line of defense against bad actors and illegal robocallers," as the proposal targets Voice over Internet Protocol technology that converts voice into digital data and transmits it over broadband connections. The FCC framed the restrictions as a national security measure aimed at preventing scam-related robocalls, and the proposal would also cover IP-enabled service providers that obtain U.S. numbers through internet-based voice services.
The FCC also announced plans to prohibit IP-enabled service providers from using equipment manufactured by companies on its list of entities considered national security risks, including Huawei and ZTE. The FCC said it would ban all Chinese laboratories from testing US electronics in December 2028, and it is considering revoking direct phone number authorisations for Chinese companies it considers security risks.
China’s foreign ministry said it firmly opposed the proposed restrictions, accusing Washington of abusing national security concerns to suppress Chinese companies. Guo Jiakun told a daily press conference, "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests," as the FCC moved to tighten rules around Chinese telecom access. The FCC also said it plans to bar IP-enabled service providers that use equipment from companies on the FCC's list that pose national security risks, including Huawei or ZTE.
The FCC added that it would ban all Chinese labs from testing US electronics in December 2028 and may also revoke direct number authorizations for Chinese companies that it deems to pose a national security risk. The FCC has previously prohibited China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States, and it is considering additional measures including blocking connections to US networks and operating data centres in the country.
Washington’s concerns about potential espionage and other security threats linked to Chinese access to American telecommunications infrastructure have grown in recent years, with the FCC tying the curbs to national security and robocall prevention. In late 2024, the US government said a Chinese state-sponsored cyber espionage group known as Salt Typhoon had stolen consumers’ call records and US call data while infiltrating telecommunications companies and infrastructure. The FBI said this year that threats from Salt Typhoon were "still very much ongoing," as the FCC’s proposal advanced toward its November 19 vote.
The FCC also added California-based Digitalsystem Technology to its list of companies considered national security risks in July, citing links to Chinese telecommunications firms and its ownership by a Chinese national. The FCC’s broader package includes barring Chinese laboratories from testing US electronics in December 2028 and considering whether to revoke direct access authorisations, while the Chinese government has consistently denied wrongdoing.

articles.title_orig: EU diplomats object to G20 photo with Lavrov, prompting US cancellation
articles.title_zh: EU diplomats object to G20 photo with Lavrov, prompting US cancellation
articles.content_orig:
The United States cancelled a planned group photo of foreign ministers from the world's 20 largest economies (G20) on Friday after several European diplomats objected to being photographed alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to walk out.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio decided to cancel the photo to avoid further controversy, according to two US officials who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the matter.
Opening the talks, Rubio looked ahead, saying he hoped for “a productive meeting.”
“We are in a critical moment — I would call it a moment of choosing, and I would say not just for my country, the United States of America, but frankly, for the world," he said.
“We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises,” he added, many posing "severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.”
The cancellation of the traditional group photo highlighted tensions within the G20, as diplomats face difficult negotiations over the war in Ukraine, the US-Israeli war against Iran, US tariffs and disputes in the South China Sea.
Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski said the cancellation of the group photo was “the right decision” by the US, telling media in Atlanta that “I am not the only one who does not want to be photographed with Lavrov.”
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said “there is no normality with Russia” but “we must exchange the controversies at the table here,” the German news agency dpa reported. He added that “we also must not send falsely optimistic signals.”
Even before the dispute over the photo, several G20 countries had raised concerns about Russia's invitation amid intensified attacks on Ukraine.
Tensions have also grown after Trump waived new sanctions on Moscow and temporarily restricted logistical and intelligence support for Kyiv, further straining US-Ukraine relations.

articles.title_orig: First Algerian troops arrive in Niger where jihadists threaten stability
articles.title_zh: First Algerian troops arrive in Niger where jihadists threaten stability
articles.content_orig:
1. President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered Algeria’s first foreign troop deployment since 1973 after Niger requested help, the presidency said Monday.
2. Units will be stationed at Madama, a former French base near the Libyan border, to guard Sonatrach oil assets and the Trans-Saharan pipeline route.
3. The move places Algerian forces in counterterrorism infrastructure vacated by France and the United States, with Russia’s Africa Corps already operating elsewhere in Niger.
Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered army units to neighboring Niger on Monday to protect energy and economic assets, the presidency said, carrying out the country’s first foreign military deployment since it sent forces to support Egypt in the 1973 Arab-Israeli war.
Both chambers of parliament approved the mission in a closed emergency session on Sunday, after Tebboune submitted the request on October 22. The Council of the Nation, the upper house, backed it with 148 of 174 senators present voting in favor, and the People’s National Assembly, the lower house, approved it by what it called an absolute majority.
Article 91 of Algeria’s constitution, added in a 2020 revision, requires two-thirds support in each chamber for troops to serve abroad. Authorities have not said how many soldiers will be sent or when.
Lawmakers authorized the deployment of National Army units to Madama, a settlement in northern Niger near the Libyan border, according to a parliamentary statement. The site is a former forward operating base that France built and used during Operation Barkhane, its decade-long counterterrorism campaign across the Sahel, the semi-arid belt stretching south of the Sahara.
The choice of base sends the clearest signal of what Algiers intends. France withdrew its roughly 1,500 troops from Niger by December 2023 after the July 2023 coup, and the United States pulled out about 1,000 personnel in 2024, abandoning a drone base near Agadez.
Algerian forces would now occupy ground that Western militaries left, in a country where roughly 100 Russian Africa Corps personnel have operated since April 2024 from a separate compound at Air Base 101 in Niamey.
No troops have crossed the border yet, a Nigerien security source said. Niger’s presidential chief of staff, General Bacharou Ibro Amadou, has been in the Kawar area of the Agadez region since October 19 and traveled to Madama to meet local military commanders to discuss plans for the base.
Algeria shares a 951-mile border with Niger and has long treated instability across it as a domestic security problem. State energy company Sonatrach is developing the Kafra oil field in northern Niger, about 53 miles from the Algerian border, through its SIPEX subsidiary, and began drilling a well there on August 13.
Niger is also the missing middle section of the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline, a project valued at about $13 billion and planned to run more than 2,500 miles to carry Nigerian gas through Niger and Algeria to European markets. Algeria broke ground on its stretch in June.
The deployment caps a fast reconciliation. Niger recalled its ambassador from Algiers in April 2025 after Algeria shot down a Malian drone near the border, joining fellow Alliance of Sahel States members Mali and Burkina Faso. The two governments restored ties in February 2026.
Niger Defense Minister Salifou Mody visited Algiers on October 20 and signed a military cooperation protocol, days before the vote.
In August, Algeria sent four Sukhoi Su-30 fighter jets and support aircraft to Niamey after a mutiny there.
The scale of Algeria’s forces frames the shift. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute reported that Algeria spent $25.4 billion on defense in 2025, the largest military budget in Africa and about 25% of government spending, the second-highest such share worldwide after Ukraine.
What Officials Are Saying: After Sunday’s vote, Senator Belkacem Boulghiti told reporters the mission would protect economic infrastructure, particularly Algerian oil facilities. “We are not sending our soldiers to wage war in Niger, but for a mission to secure economic infrastructure,” he said, describing the step as an adaptation of Algeria’s doctrine to conditions in the Sahel.
